content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To write tengwar, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Research the specific mode for the English language (2 hours)
Step 2. Purchase a high-quality calligraphy nib (45 minutes)
Step 3. Memorize the primary four series of consonants (3 hours)
Step 4. Study the placement of Tehtar above the Tengwa (1 hour)
Step 5. Grind a solid ink stick into liquid (20 minutes)
Step 6. Select a heavy-weight parchment paper (10 minutes)
Step 7. Download a reference chart for the Feanorian letters (5 minutes)
Step 8. Clear a wide, flat workspace (15 minutes)
Step 9. Practice the basic vertical stem stroke (30 minutes)
Step 10. Write out a full stanza of the Namárië poem (2 hours)
Step 11. Print the reference chart for physical use (2 minutes)
Step 12. Draft the final composition in light pencil (4 hours)
Step 13. Map out the phonemes of your chosen text (1 hour)
Step 14. Adjust the slant of the writing desk (5 minutes)
Step 15. Mix a drop of gum arabic into the ink (5 minutes)
Step 16. Secure the nib into the pen holder (1 minute)
Step 17. Apply gold leaf to the initial capital letters (6 hours)
Step 18. Set up a dedicated lamp for task lighting (10 minutes)
Step 19. Practice the curved "bow" shapes of the letters (1 hour)
Step 20. Trace the outlines of the characters on scrap paper (2 hours)
Step 21. Review the rules for double consonants (40 minutes)
Step 22. Test the ink flow on a small corner of parchment (3 minutes)
Step 23. Execute the final ink strokes on the parchment (5 hours)
Step 24. Clean the workspace and store materials (20 minutes)
Step 25. Learn the values of the Grade 1 and 2 characters (2 hours)
Step 26. Practice the "carrier" symbols for independent vowels (45 minutes)
Step 27. Perform a final proofread of the phonetic transcription (30 minutes)
Step 28. Cut the parchment to the desired dimensions (15 minutes)
Step 29. Rule horizontal guidelines using a T-square (30 minutes)
Step 30. Watch a tutorial on proper pen angle (25 minutes)
Step 31. Identify the vowels in the source text (15 minutes)
Step 32. Tape the parchment to the drawing board (5 minutes)
Step 33. Learn the difference between Telco and Luva (1.5 hours)
Step 34. Practice drawing the Tehtar marks (50 minutes)
Step 35. Prepare a damp cloth for cleaning the nib (2 minutes)
Step 36. Recite the letters aloud to ensure phonetic accuracy (1 hour)
Step 37. Dip the pen into the prepared ink (10 seconds)
Step 38. Travel to a specialty stationery store (1 hour)
Step 39. Combine consonants and vowels in a practice draft (2 hours)
Step 40. Purchase a set of Tolkien’s linguistic guides (30 minutes)
